rule.name: Clarifications
rule.description: - **Review for Faithfulness**: Checks for development faithfulness to existing tests MUST occur almost continuously, approximately every 3-4 task updates.

rule.name: I. Architecture: CLI-Centric
rule.description: All core functionality MUST be accessible and usable via a Command Line Interface (CLI). Design SHOULD prioritize shell-friendly operations, minimal dependencies, and local-first execution. Modularity and extensibility SHOULD be considered for future phases (Phase 4-5) but MUST NOT introduce complexity that hinders CLI-centricity in earlier phases.

rule.name: II. Testing: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
rule.description: Test-Driven Development (TDD) is MANDATORY. Tests MUST be written before implementation code. The development cycle MUST follow the Red-Green-Refactor pattern:

rule.name: III. Code Quality: Consistent and Maintainable
rule.description: Code MUST adhere to established style guides and best practices for the language and tools used (e.g., shell scripting conventions, Python PEP 8). Readability, clarity, and maintainability MUST be prioritized. Code duplication SHOULD be minimized. Automated linting and formatting tools SHOULD be used to enforce consistency.

rule.name: III.B. CLI Alias Consistency (NEW - Phase 3b)
rule.description: The shell alias file (`scripts/aliases.sh`) and the Copilot CLI alias file (`.github/copilot-aliases.json`) MUST be kept in sync on every commit. Any change to one file requires a corresponding update to the other, ensuring all CLI and Copilot command aliases remain consistent and up-to-date. Pre-commit hooks or CI checks SHOULD enforce this synchronization.

rule.name: III.C. Cross-Platform Portability: Platform-Specific Metadata Exclusion (NEW - Phase 3b)
rule.description: Platform-specific metadata files (e.g., Windows `Zone.Identifier` files, macOS `.DS_Store`) MUST be excluded from version control via `.gitignore`. These files MUST NOT be committed to the repository, as they prevent proper checkout on other platforms. The `.gitignore` file MUST include patterns for all known platform metadata: `*:Zone.Identifier` (Windows), `.DS_Store` (macOS), `Thumbs.db` (Windows), and similar OS-generated files. Developers working across Windows, macOS, and Linux environments MUST ensure their local `.gitignore` configuration matches the repository's `.gitignore`, or use a global config: `git config --global core.excludesFile ~/.gitignore_global`. Pre-commit hooks SHOULD validate that no platform metadata files are staged before commit.

rule.name: IV. CI Gating: Automated Verification
rule.description: All changes MUST pass automated checks (e.g., linting, testing, security scans, constitutional compliance) before merging into the main branch. These checks MUST be executable locally via the CLI. In Phase 2, 'CI pipelines' refer primarily to these local CLI-based checks providing rapid feedback. Remote CI system integrations providing similar feedback will be implemented in later phases (Phase 3+). Blocking failures SHOULD prevent merging, while non-blocking issues SHOULD be reported for review and justification.

rule.name: V. Security: Proactive and Defense-in-Depth
rule.description: Security considerations MUST be integrated into all phases of development, from design to deployment. Code MUST be written to prevent common vulnerabilities (e.g., injection, unauthorized access, privilege escalation). All external dependencies MUST be vetted for known security issues. Local file system access and command execution MUST adhere to the principle of least privilege. Security scans SHOULD be part of CI gating.

rule.name: VI. Performance: Efficient and Responsive
rule.description: CLI commands MUST execute quickly and efficiently, minimizing resource consumption (CPU, memory, disk I/O). Operations on local files MUST be optimized for speed. Any user-perceptible delays SHOULD be communicated to the user. Benchmarking SHOULD be used to identify and address performance bottlenecks.

rule.name: VII. Documentation: Clear and Up-to-Date
rule.description: All CLI commands, configuration options, architectural decisions, and public APIs MUST be clearly and comprehensively documented. Documentation MUST be kept up-to-date with code changes. In-code comments SHOULD explain complex logic, assumptions, and workarounds. User-facing documentation SHOULD include examples and usage guides.

rule.name: VIII. Dependencies: Managed, Minimal, and Zero for Testing
rule.description: External dependencies MUST be carefully selected, actively managed, and kept to an absolute minimum. Each dependency MUST have a clear purpose and SHOULD be thoroughly vetted for security, stability, and licensing. Dependency updates SHOULD be performed regularly and automatically where feasible. The project MUST NOT introduce unnecessary external network calls.

rule.name: IX. Amendment and Governance: Transparent and Controlled
rule.description: The project constitution is a living document that MUST be maintained and evolved through a transparent process. Amendments MUST follow a defined workflow including proposal, discussion, review, and ratification by designated maintainers. All changes to the constitution MUST include a migration plan if they introduce breaking changes or require significant refactoring.

rule.name: Development Workflow
rule.description: All development activities, including design, implementation, and review, MUST adhere to the principles outlined in this constitution. **All implementation work MUST follow the Test-Driven Development (TDD) process.** Proposed changes SHOULD be evaluated for constitutional compliance during the code review process. Tools like SpecFarm SHOULD be utilized to provide automated feedback on adherence and drift.

rule.name: X. Open-Core & Freemium Governance (Strategic Plan)

rule.name: Enforcement
rule.description: - **Module Integrity Checks**: Pre-commit hooks and CI gates MUST validate module function exports using `tests/e2e/test_function_exports.sh`. Silent deletion of critical functions is a HARD BLOCK and MUST prevent commits.

rule.name: Amendment Workflow
rule.description: Proposals to amend this Constitution MUST be submitted as a pull request to the main branch.
